subject: Urgent: Riverfront - post-upgrade latency & error spike
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@riverfront.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production regression after v4.2 quant profile cutover - immediate impact

Ben / Marissa,

We pushed Redwood v4.2 (quant profile qv2a) on Saturday during the maintenance window. Since then our production tail latency (p99) has tripled and we are seeing intermittent 5xx errors on the inference path. Throughput is down ~35% vs baseline which is throttling our checkout flow.

Attached are the p99 timelines and an SRE screenshot showing the error distribution. Our ops team confirmed no infra changes on our side — everything points to the model variant/quant change. This is customer-impacting for our marketplace and leadership is asking for an ETA on rollback or mitigation within the next 6 hours.

Please advise immediately. We are ready to take a short maintenance window if that helps.

Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Engineering, Riverfront Logistics
alex.morgan@riverfront.com

Attachments: riverfront_p99_offsets.csv, sre_screenshot_0601.png
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@riverfront.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production regression after v4.2 quant profile cutover - immediate impact

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the data. I’m really sorry you’re seeing this.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I’ve escalated to our on-call incident lead and looped in Marissa (AE) and Irene (Customer Success) for exec coordination.
- We will propose a rollback to the previous quant profile (qv1-compatible) as a first action, timeline ~30–45 minutes to test and validate.
- If rollback isn’t acceptable, we’ll run a targeted canary with reduced batch sizes and revert KV cache heuristics for your account only.

Can you confirm whether a 30–45 minute maintenance window is okay now? If so, we’ll schedule the rollback and share a live incident doc (link incoming).

I’ll coordinate the exec bridge if leadership needs to join.

—Ben

Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production regression after v4.2 quant profile cutover - Riverfront escalation

Forwarding Riverfront details — p99 spike + 35% throughput drop after our v4.2 qprofile. They attached p99 CSV and an SRE screenshot.

Proposed internal ask:
1) Approve account-scoped rollback to previous quant profile (qv1) as immediate mitigation (target 30–45m).
2) If rollback is required, offer a one-time SLA credit and a short exec bridge with Riverfront CTO.
3) Post-rollback: run a joint telemetry session to identify whether kernel selection or KV-cache decay caused the regression; capture token-level traces.

Irene — can you own the exec bridge / credit conversation? Marissa — can you confirm any contractual constraints on rollback windows for RF-4821? Rishi — please prep C-level notification copy if we need to escalate.

Thanks — Ben
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production regression after v4.2 quant profile cutover - Riverfront escalation

Ben / team — agreed. Immediate rollback on account-scoped config is fine. Contract allows emergency mitigations for production-impacting regressions; we can attach a one-off credit up to 2% of monthly commit. Irene, please schedule the bridge with Riverfront CTO and escalate to CS leadership.

I’ll coordinate with Solutions to ensure we capture the exact model variant and quant profile used in the cutover (include model hash, compiled kernel set, and qprofile id). After rollback, we’ll run a 2-hour validated canary on the old profile before reattempting any optimized qprofile.

Action items assigned:
- Irene: schedule 09:30 bridge and confirm Riverfront approval for maintenance window.
- Ben: confirm rollback timeline with on-call and share incident doc (INC-9072).
- Rishi: prepare C-level note (subject: Riverfront production regression) in case their execs want a briefing.

Marissa Cole

Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production regression after v4.2 quant profile cutover - immediate impact

Alex — update from our side: the on-call ops team validated the regression locally and completed an account-scoped rollback to qv1 at 10:22 PDT. Initial validation shows p99 returning to baseline and error rate dropping to normal. We left qv2a in a canary with reduced batch size to collect traces.

Next steps we propose:
- 11:15 PDT live bridge (30 min) to review post-rollback telemetry and agree next safe rollout approach. Link to incident doc: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9072
- We will provide a detailed postmortem within 48 hours including kernel-selection logs and token-level KV cache traces.
- As a gesture, Redwood will apply the emergency credit discussed (2% of june committed spend) — Irene will follow up with the formal credit note and DocuSign link if needed.

Please confirm you can join the 11:15 bridge and if you need us to extend the maintenance window. Again, very sorry for the disruption — we’ll treat this as high priority until the RC is closed.

—Ben
